At the rice mill office in his small town, Tushar had noticed something in the weighing slips that troubled him, and he carried it for a week. Then on Sunday he took the local bus to see Minakshi, an old teacher's daughter who now worked at a firm in the next district.
Over tea at the bus-stand stall, he kept it general. "Suppose someone noticed figures that looked altered. How did you decide what to do in your job?"
Minakshi stirred her tea. "When it happened to me, I wrote down only what I had seen, read our policy and used the route it named. I never told anyone outside."
Tushar nodded. He had not said one name or number, and he felt steadier on the ride home.

What was Tushar feeling as he asked his general question?
qa.a: Tushar was uneasy and unsure, having carried the worry for a week, but relieved to be able to talk.

qa.q: What could Tushar do next after the talk with Minakshi?
qa.a: Tushar could read the mill's policy, write down what he saw with dates, and use the official route it names.

qa.q: How might Minakshi have felt hearing Tushar's question?
qa.a: Minakshi probably recognised the situation from her own experience and was glad to share what she had learned.

grounding: The passage shows an employee talking in general terms to a trusted mentor at another firm, learning how similar situations were handled, and revealing no confidential details.

On Saturday morning in a café in Melbourne, Yosef stirred his coffee and wondered how to ask without saying too much. Bao had supervised his internship three years ago and now worked at a different engineering firm across the city.
'Hypothetically,' Yosef said, 'if you saw test results being rounded up in a report, just enough to pass, what would you do?'
Bao didn't ask which project or which client. 'Hypothetically, I'd first make sure I understood the testing standard. Then I'd write down what I saw and take it to my manager, and if that went nowhere, to the quality team.' She paused. 'At my first job, I waited six months. That was too long.'
Yosef nodded. He hadn't named the company, the client or anyone involved, and he left with a plan and a steadier stomach.

qa.a: At a different engineering firm across the city.
It suggests Yosef had been anxious and unsure, and felt calmer after hearing how an experienced person would handle it.

qa.q: Which part of Yosef's approach protected his company's confidentiality?
qa.a: He spoke only hypothetically and never named the company, the client or anyone involved, so he got advice without leaking details.

qa.q: How might Bao feel being asked?
qa.a: Bao seems glad to help and honest about waiting too long at her first job, perhaps hoping Yosef won't repeat that.

grounding: It shows an employee talking in general terms to a mentor at another firm to test judgement without leaking confidential details.

The alumni evening at the engineering college was loud, so Kiran steered Shalini ma'am, her old project guide who now ran a consulting firm, to a quiet corner near the notice board.
'Can I ask something in general terms?' Kiran said. 'Nothing I can name.'
'Go on.'
'If a team keeps billing clients for training hours that didn't happen, and everyone says that's normal, how do people handle it?'
Shalini didn't ask for names. She told Kiran about two people she had worked with: one who stayed silent and later regretted it, and one who wrote a factual note to the company's ethics officer and was, eventually, thanked. 'Know your company's reporting route before you do anything,' she said. 'And keep notes.'
Kiran went home without having named a single person or client, but clearer about the next step.

qa.q: Where did Kiran steer Shalini to talk?
qa.a: To a quiet corner near the notice board.

qa.q: How did Kiran seem to feel going home?
qa.a: Kiran felt clearer and less alone, with a next step instead of a vague unease.

qa.q: According to Shalini, what should Kiran find out first, and why?
qa.a: The company's reporting route, so any concern goes through the proper channel, backed by factual notes.

qa.q: How might Shalini see Kiran's careful way of asking?
qa.a: Shalini likely respects that Kiran kept names and clients private, which let her share experience without risking confidences.

grounding: It shows an employee consulting a mentor outside the company in general terms to test judgement without leaking confidential details.
